reason: This bullet defines the Patient role; 'Patient: The patient who is receiving care' is circular. D-2 (recommended B) also allows 'individual' here.

'Community Resource Platform' is the page's own bolded, defined actor label (line 33) used in Title Case throughout the page; changing one table cell leaves the definition and line 21 unchanged and breaks the page's internal consistency. The rulebook's own suggestion for this pattern is 'coordination platform (CP)', which would misstate the role (here the platform is the referral source system, not an intermediary's CP). A page-wide rename belongs in glossary_feedback, not a single-cell edit.
This bullet defines the 'Individual/Patient' role, so 'A patient or an authorized representative...' is circular; D-2 (recommended B) explicitly keeps 'person' on the self-referral page.
Same definition bullet as @2179: role definition on the self-referral page where D-2 keeps 'person'. 'representative of a patient' also narrows the person before they are a subject of care.

QuestionnaireResponse.author search parameter: the author is normally a practitioner, device or organization, not the patient. 'particular patient' changes the meaning of the search documentation; the packet itself marks it keep.

Task.requester search parameter: the requester is a practitioner or organization that initiated the task, and the next sentence says it is used to monitor tasks 'initiated by a particular system'. 'organization or patient' misdescribes the FHIR element.
Same QuestionnaireResponse.author documentation as @171550: the author may be a practitioner, so 'particular patient' alters meaning.

The subject is 'systems that originate requests for service may sometimes also be recipients of requests for service': a deliberate parallel about systems. 'Referral target' is an organizational actor in the glossary, and the domain notes say not to recast system roles as referral source/target; the swap also breaks the originate/recipient pairing.
Same Task.requester documentation as @196113: requester is a practitioner, organization or system, not a patient.

'Recipient' here is shorthand for the receiving system ('receivers', 'referral recipient systems', 'local persistence or FHIR server capabilities'), and 'Referral Recipient' is the CapabilityStatement's name. The glossary's referral target is an organizational actor, so 'the referral target is a light referral recipient that doesn't have ... FHIR server capabilities' mixes actor kinds; per the domain notes, system roles are left alone.
